Each extractor may produce different results depending on the document structure — try different options and compare the output. Important: RAG only uses text. If your PDF contains images with text (scanned documents, diagrams), you must use an OCR-capable extractor like EasyOCR to convert those images into text that RAG can use. Without OCR, images are ignored.

retriever.description: Select your retrieval paradigm. The retriever will search through your documents and return the most relevant chunks.

howItWorks.step1: Select the documents you want the assistant to use.
howItWorks.step2: Documents are split into smaller chunks (chunking) to make retrieval efficient.
howItWorks.step3: A retriever finds the most relevant chunks for your question.
howItWorks.step4: The LLM generates an answer using those chunks and the selected prompt template.

chunking.point1: Chunking splits documents into smaller pieces that can be searched.
chunking.point2: Too small chunks: retrieval can miss context and answers may feel fragmented.
chunking.point3: Too large chunks: retrieval can bring extra noise and answers may be slower (more tokens).
chunking.point4: Overlap helps keep context between chunks, but increases repetition.
chunking.title: Chunking

documents.point1: Your documents are the knowledge base: the assistant can only use what it can retrieve from them.
documents.point2: Upload clear, well-structured files (PDF, TXT, etc.) for best results.
documents.point3: Currently, only text-based documents are supported. Images, audio, and video are not yet supported.
documents.title: Documents

llm.point1: The LLM writes the final answer using the retrieved chunks.
llm.point2: Larger models usually answer better, but can be slower and costlier.
llm.point3: If you need speed, start with a smaller model and iterate.
llm.title: Language Model (LLM)

prompt.point1: Prompts control the tone, format, and what the model should focus on.
prompt.point2: If answers are too long/short or lack structure, try another template or refine the prompt.
prompt.title: Prompt template

retriever.point1: The retriever decides which chunks are sent to the LLM.
retriever.point2: Sparse (keyword-based): great for exact terms like IDs, product names, or code; usually fast.
retriever.point3: Sparse limitation: struggles with synonyms and heavily paraphrased questions.
retriever.point4: Dense (semantic): better for natural language and paraphrases; searches by meaning.
retriever.point5: Dense limitation: can return ‘similar’ but not exact matches, and may be slower.
retriever.title: Retriever (Sparse vs Dense)

rightPanel.subtitle: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) helps the model answer using your documents.

tips.tip1: If answers miss context, try larger chunks or more overlap.
tips.tip2: If answers feel too generic, try smaller chunks or adjust the retriever model.
tips.tip3: Choose a prompt template that matches your domain and tone.

rightPanel.title: RAG basics
